links.outcome: Hallucinated and unfaithful citations in LLM reports versus human reports
links.effect: Human reports contained no hallucinated (p < 0.001) or unfaithful (p < 0.001) citations, unlike LLM reports.
links.quote: Unlike LLMs, human reports contained no hallucinated (p < 0.001) or unfaithful (p < 0.001) citations.

links.outcome: LLM reports contain hallucinated citations that clinicians would need to verify before acting
links.effect: LLM reports contained hallucinated and unfaithful citations while human reports had none (p < 0.001 for both).
links.quote: Unlike LLMs, human reports contained no hallucinated (p < 0.001) or unfaithful (p < 0.001) citations.

links.outcome: Correlation between physician satisfaction and objective report quality
links.effect: No meaningful correlation between physician satisfaction and objective measures of report quality, so satisfaction is not a good quality measure.
links.quote: However, no meaningful correlation was identified between physician satisfaction and objective measures of report quality.

screen.reason: Evaluates the accuracy, reliability, citations, and physician satisfaction of LLM-generated reports versus human researcher reports on complex medical queries without testing a specific organizational guardrail or deployment practice.
